subtopics.title: Growth Against Development — Two Different Questions

questions.question: Economic growth is measured by:
options: The annual percentage change in real GDP — real, so inflation cannot masquerade as progress
The number of new businesses registered

questions.question: With population growing about 1,5 percent a year, South African real GDP growth of 1 percent means:
options: The average person is getting poorer even as the economy grows

questions.question: The three dimensions of the HDI are:
options: A long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living

questions.question: "Growth without development" describes:
options: A country whose HDI rises while GDP falls
A country with no natural resources
An economy expanding through capital-intensive exports while employment, schooling and life expectancy stand still — the resource-enclave pattern

questions.question: Demand-side approaches raise growth by:
options: Raising spending — C, I, G and X — and trusting the multiplier to translate it into income and jobs

questions.question: Grants are powerful spending fuel because:
options: They are paid in foreign currency
The poor's high marginal propensity to consume sends almost every grant rand straight into spending

questions.question: The IMPORT wall against South African stimulus is that:
options: A high marginal propensity to import leaks a large slice of any stimulus abroad — the small-multiplier problem

questions.question: The summary evaluation of demand-side measures is that they:
options: Treat symptoms quickly and visibly, but where the binding constraints are on the supply side they buy relief, not transformation

questions.question: Supply-side approaches aim to:
options: Shift the production possibility frontier outward by raising the economy's capacity to produce

questions.question: Infrastructure failure "taxes the whole economy at once" because:
options: Unreliable electricity, ports and rail raise every producer's costs simultaneously

questions.question: The main weaknesses of supply-side measures are that they are:
options: Slow to pay off, socially regressive in the short run, and dependent on the very state capacity whose failures are well known

questions.question: The mature evaluation of the two approaches is:
options: Sequencing and proportion — demand-side protects people through the present while supply-side decides whether the future is bigger; do both in proportion

subtopics.title: South Africa's Endeavours and the North-South Divide

questions.question: South Africa's growth strategies in correct order are:
The honest verdict on South Africa's endeavours is:
options: Every target of every plan was met
Macro stability and the social wage are real achievements, but growth has trailed population and the named constraints — electricity, logistics, skills, state capacity — remain

questions.question: A mechanism that keeps the north-south gap open is:
options: The South's control of world financial institutions
Free technology transfer to the South
Tariff structures that tax processed goods more than raw ones, discouraging southern industrialisation
The North's dependence on southern manufactured exports

questions.question: South Africa "sits astride the line" because it is:
options: Southern in poverty and history yet northern in financial sophistication and industrial base — a dual character

subtopics.title: The Payslip and the Report Card

questions.question: The first family — income up, children out of school, winters of coughing — shows:
options: Growth without development — money up, life not

questions.question: "A payslip that grows slower than the family does is a pay cut wearing a smile" is the household version of:
options: Real GDP per capita falling when growth trails population growth

questions.question: The country-scale report card that grades long life, learning and affordable living is:
The honest two-fact sentence about South Africa is:
options: High growth and a poor report card
No growth and no development since 1994
The world's best payslip and report card
A payslip that has barely kept up with the family's size, and a report card better than the payslip explains — because grants, clinics and housing did real work

subtopics.title: Feed the Fire or Build the Stove

questions.question: "Feeding the fire" stands for:
options: Demand-side policy — money into pockets, spent and re-spent, warmth spreading through the multiplier

questions.question: "Pour money in when the pots are already full and you get higher prices" is the household version of:
options: Stimulus at full capacity multiplying inflation instead of output

questions.question: The stove's slowness is described as "the price of its permanence" because:
options: Schools, skills and infrastructure take years to build but then raise production every day, forever

questions.question: The proportion sentence concludes:
options: Only build the stove, whatever the hunger
Fires and stoves are unrelated to policy
Feed the fire enough to hold everyone through the present, and never stop building the stove

questions.question: The suburb's gate tariff — raw things nearly free, manufactured things taxed — matters because:
options: It discourages the street from ever owning a stove — southern industrialisation is penalised at the gate
It only affects the suburb's own producers
It is set by the street's families

questions.question: "None of this needs a villain" means:
options: The divide persists through structural mechanisms — terms of trade, debt in foreign currency, tariff escalation, brain drain — not personal malice
The suburb secretly plans the street's poverty

questions.question: Evidence that "the story is no longer only the gap" includes:
options: The end of all world trade
The street refusing to trade at all
East Asia's rise, south-south trade and the AfCFTA, and remittances outweighing aid

questions.question: South Africa as "the corner house" must therefore:
options: Choose the suburb and forget the street
Choose the street and abandon its industry
Wait for the map to redraw itself
Hold both tasks at once — build the stove of growth while keeping the fire of development burning under everyone
